summary: The root رغد (raghd) describes something plentiful, easy, and unstraitened, like an ample life or abundant sustenance. It implies a state of comfort and ease, free from hardship or fatigue.
lane: رَغْدٌ ذ , applied to property, or water, or life, or herbage, Plentiful; that does not cause one fatigue. (L.) [Being originally an inf. n., it is used without variation as a masc. and fem. and sing. and pl. epithet; as also .] You say عَيْشٌ رَغْدٌ and and and (A, Msb) and , (Lh, TA,) and مَعِيشَةٌ , (A,) Life that is ample in its means or circumstances, unstraitened, or plentiful, (Lh, A, Msb,) and easy, (Lh, * Msb,) and pleasant. (A, Msb.) And غِيشَةٌ رَغْدٌ and A mode of life ample in its means or circumstances, unstraitened, or plentiful, [ and easy, ] and pleasant. (S, A, K.) And قَوْمٌ , (A, L, K,) or رَغْدٌ , (JK,) and نِسْوَةٌ , (A, L, K,) or نِسَآءٌ رَغْدٌ , (JK,) People, and women, in a state of life ample in its means or circumstances, &c.; (JK, A, K;) or having abundance of herbage, or of the goods, conveniences, or comforts, of life, and having camels abounding with milk. (L.)
